title: Sampling Methods & Weight Calibration Diagnostic
description: Assess proficiency in multi-stage cluster sampling, multiplier calculation, stratification, and sample weighting.

questions.question: In a two-stage stratified sampling design, what is the base sampling weight (multiplier) of a selected household?
options: The product of the probabilities of selection at both stages
The inverse of the joint inclusion probability of the primary and secondary stage units
The total population divided by the total number of primary sampling units
The ratio of the sample mean to the population mean
questions.explanation: The base sampling weight (multiplier) is the inverse of the inclusion probability (Horvitz-Thompson estimator): w_ij = 1 / (P(PSU_i) * P(SSU_ij | PSU_i)).

questions.question: What is the primary objective of Neyman (optimum) allocation in stratified random sampling?
options: To ensure an equal number of sample units are chosen from every stratum
To minimise the variance of the estimated mean for a fixed overall sample size when stratum variances differ
To maximise the response rate in difficult geographic strata
To eliminate non-sampling errors across field investigators
questions.explanation: Neyman allocation allocates sample sizes proportionally to N_h * S_h (stratum size multiplied by stratum standard deviation), which mathematically minimises the variance of the estimator under a fixed total sample size.

questions.question: What is the Design Effect (DEFF) of a cluster sampling design when the intraclass correlation coefficient (rho) is positive?
options: DEFF is strictly equal to 1
DEFF is less than 1, indicating higher precision than simple random sampling
DEFF is greater than 1, indicating lower precision than simple random sampling of the same size
DEFF cannot be computed when clusters have unequal sizes
questions.explanation: DEFF = 1 + (m - 1)*rho. When rho > 0 and cluster size m > 1, DEFF > 1. This means cluster sampling has a larger variance (standard error) than an SRS of the same total sample size.

questions.question: When non-response occurs in household surveys, which technique is standardly applied to prevent non-response bias?
options: Arbitrarily substituting the non-responding household with their next-door neighbour
Deleting the entire primary sampling unit from the analysis
Re-weighting responding households using response propensity or weighting classes within strata
Assigning a zero value to all missing household variables
questions.explanation: Standard official statistical practice uses weighting class adjustments or response propensity re-weighting. Arbitrary substitution in the field introduces severe selection bias and violates probability sampling.

title: Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) Concepts & Indicator Derivation
description: Evaluate knowledge of activity status codes, reference periods (ps+ss vs CWS), and labour market ratios.

questions.question: Under the Usual Principal Status (UPS) approach in PLFS, what reference period is considered to determine a person's principal activity?
options: The preceding 7 days prior to the date of survey
The major time criterion (183 days or more) during the 365 days preceding the date of survey
The exact day prior to the interview
The last completed financial quarter
questions.explanation: The Usual Principal Status classifies an individual based on the activity on which they spent a relatively long time (major time criterion) during the 365 days preceding the date of survey.

questions.question: How is the Worker Population Ratio (WPR) mathematically defined in official reports?
options: (Total employed persons / Total labour force) * 100
(Total unemployed persons / Total population) * 100
(Total employed persons / Total population) * 100
(Total labour force / Total working-age population) * 100
questions.explanation: Worker Population Ratio (WPR) is defined as the percentage of employed persons in the total population: (Employed / Total Population) * 100.

questions.question: In the Current Weekly Status (CWS) approach, what is the minimum duration of work in the reference week required to be classified as employed?
options: At least 40 hours during the 7 days
At least 1 hour on at least one day during the 7 days
At least 4 hours on any single day
At least half a day on every working day
questions.explanation: Following ILO standards, in the Current Weekly Status (CWS), a person is considered employed if they worked for at least 1 hour on at least 1 day during the 7-day reference period.

title: Python for Statistical Wrangling & Pipeline Verification
description: Assess proficiency in Pandas DataFrame transformations, memory optimisation, and microdata processing.

questions.question: Which Pandas operation is the most efficient and idiomatically correct way to calculate weighted averages across survey strata?
options: A Python for-loop iterating over df.iterrows() and appending to a list
df.groupby('stratum').apply(lambda g: (g['value'] * g['weight']).sum() / g['weight'].sum())
Using eval() in a recursive function
Converting the entire DataFrame into a nested Python dictionary first
questions.explanation: Using groupby with a vectorised weighted calculation avoids slow row-by-row iteration (iterrows is notoriously slow on large microdata).

questions.question: When parsing a fixed-width text file (.dat / .txt) from an official statistical agency, which Pandas function should be used?
options: pd.read_csv() with delimiter='	'
pd.read_fwf() specifying colspecs or widths
pd.read_table() with regex split
pd.read_excel()
questions.explanation: pd.read_fwf() (read fixed-width formatted lines) is built specifically for positional columns with fixed character widths, which is the standard format for legacy census and NSS survey releases.

questions.question: How can memory footprint be drastically reduced when loading large survey datasets with millions of rows and categorical responses?
options: Converting repetitive string columns (e.g., state codes, gender, sector) to the 'category' dtype
Increasing the pagefile size in Windows
Reading each column as an object dtype
Splitting the data into 100 individual CSV files
questions.explanation: Converting low-cardinality string columns to category dtype replaces large string pointers with integer codes internally, often reducing memory usage by 70-80%.

title: Data Governance, Anonymisation & DPDP Act Compliance
description: Assess comprehension of statistical disclosure control, respondent confidentiality, and data ethics.

questions.question: What is the primary rule of k-anonymity when preparing public-use microdata files?
options: Every dataset must contain at least k variables
Each combination of quasi-identifiers (e.g. age, gender, postal code) must match at least k individuals in the dataset
No respondent may be surveyed more than k times in a decade
The sample size must be a multiple of k
questions.explanation: k-anonymity guarantees that each record cannot be distinguished from at least k - 1 other individuals sharing the same quasi-identifiers, making individual re-identification improbable.

questions.question: Under the UN Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics, what must be done with data collected for statistical compilation?
options: It can be shared with law enforcement and tax authorities for prosecution
It must be sold to commercial entities to recoup survey costs
It is strictly confidential and used exclusively for statistical purposes
It must include respondent names and contact numbers in open datasets
questions.explanation: Principle 6 of UN-FPOS mandates that individual data collected by statistical agencies for compilation, whether referring to natural or legal persons, are strictly confidential and used exclusively for statistical purposes.
